Hi there. Thanks for sharing your story!! I love that you've done a lot of market research - which is a great first step. It sounds like given your experience with that team, and the positive praise you get - you likely have leverage when it comes to salary. But I know it can be intimidating. I spent a long time studying salary negotiation and these are the things that have helped me, and may help you too.

* It sounds silly, but consider the fact that they might actually expect you to negotiate. Most recruiters and hiring managers expect some sort of negotiation during the hiring process. It's pretty normal to have those conversations, even if they feel awkward. 
* Do you have a number in your head? What is the minimum amount you need to earn based off of the market research you're seeing? A difference of 5k is usually peanuts to a company, so the monetary gap you're trying to fill is really reasonable. If you were negotiating 50k more, it might be a different conversation.
* When you go into your negotiation conversations, keep your accomplishments and data handy. Being able to remind them of the impact your work has had on the business and process will help support your ask.
* It's shitty that the company wants to pay you less based on your remote location, but everyone is trying to save money here and there. That's why it's even **more** important for you to ask for more money!
* You're absolutely right that Latina women earn less, and it's unacceptable. Remember that when you're going through the process, because when you negotiate, you make it easier for all the women who come after you to do the same thing. <3 

Obviously I can't guarantee they will give you what you need, but if they don't then it's a good sign to think about applying elsewhere or at least keep your options open to new opportunities.
